questions.question: Engine belts should be:
questions.explanation: Check your engine belts for tightness and wear. Each belt needs the right amount of tightness for your vehicle. Learn what is right for your vehicle.

questions.question: If a steering axle does not have enough weight, it can cause:
questions.explanation: Cargo weight must be balanced in your vehicle. If cargo is too far back, the front axle becomes too light. This means the front wheels may not grip the road well enough for safe steering.

questions.question: A vehicle stopped at a green light may mean the driver:

options.text: Does not know the rules of the road.

questions.explanation: Watch other drivers for signs of impairment. Drivers who have used alcohol, drugs, or are tired or sick can be dangerous. Stopping at a green light is a sign a driver may be impaired.

questions.question: What is the Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR)?

options.text: The maximum allowed weight of a vehicle with its cargo
The minimum allowed weight of a trailer
The maximum allowed weight of a trailer with its cargo
The maximum allowed weight of just a tractor

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum allowed weight of a vehicle with its cargo
questions.explanation: Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW) is the total weight of a vehicle plus its load. GVWR is the maximum weight allowed for a vehicle and cargo as set by the manufacturer.

questions.question: The emergency air line:

options.text: Is controlled by the foot brake.
Is connected to the relay valves.
Supplies air to the trailer air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Supplies air to the trailer air tanks.
questions.explanation: The emergency air line (supply line) does two things. It supplies air to the trailer air tanks on combination vehicles. It also controls the emergency brakes.

questions.question: When driving down a steep grade, you should:

options.text: Use your brakes the entire way down.
Shift into a higher gear to slow down.
Shift into lower gears to slow down.
Put the truck in neutral to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift into lower gears to slow down.
questions.explanation: On a steep grade, use the engine to slow down. Only use your brakes a little to prevent overheating.

questions.question: What can happen if you use parking brakes in wet, freezing weather?

options.text: The brakes may freeze and the vehicle cannot move.
The brakes may suddenly release by themselves.
The brakes may become too smooth to use.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes may freeze and the vehicle cannot move.
questions.explanation: Do not use parking brakes in wet, freezing weather. The brakes can freeze in place, leaving the vehicle stuck.

questions.question: What comes out when you drain an air tank?
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks have drains to remove water and compressor oil. If these buildup in the brake system, they can damage the brakes.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Move quickly before other vehicles get in your way.
Move slowly in case another vehicle is in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move slowly in case another vehicle is in the lane.
questions.explanation: Change lanes slowly and smoothly. This gives drivers you did not see time to move or honk their horns. Always use your turn signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: If a tire fails while driving, you should:

options.text: Do not brake and let the vehicle slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not brake and let the vehicle slow down.
questions.explanation: If a tire fails, grip the steering wheel firmly. Do not use the brakes. Let the vehicle slow down on its own. When it slows, brake gently, move to the side of the road, and stop.

questions.question: A cargo cover that flaps while you are driving:

options.text: Lets air reach the cargo to keep it cool.

questions.explanation: Cargo covers should not flap in the wind. A flapping cover can tear loose and fall off. This exposes your cargo and may block your view or other drivers' views.

questions.question: An air supply control lever should be in its "normal" position when you are:
questions.explanation: Some older vehicles have air supply controls that use levers instead of knobs. When the air supply control is in the "normal" position, it is set correctly for pulling a trailer.

questions.question: If another vehicle is tailgating you, you should:
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, create more space ahead of your vehicle. This makes it easier for them to pass you. Do not drive faster. The other driver may just tailgate you at the higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: Using a helper when backing up is:
questions.explanation: When backing up, always use a helper. They can watch your blind spots and warn you of hazards. The helper should stand near the back of the vehicle where you can see them.

questions.question: If a vehicle has power steering, check the hoses for:
questions.explanation: When checking a power steering system, look at the hoses, pumps, and fluid level. Look especially for leaks in the hoses.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a warning sign of fatigue?
questions.explanation: Warning signs of fatigue include trouble focusing, frequent blinking, heavy eyelids, repeated yawning, rubbing your eyes, daydreaming, trouble remembering recent miles, missing exits or signs, trouble keeping your head up, drifting from your lane, following too closely, and feeling restless or irritable.

questions.question: The trailer hand valve should be used to:

options.text: Check the connection between the trailer and tractor.
Test the lights on the trailer.

questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve (also called the trolley valve or Johnson bar) controls the trailer brakes. Use it only to test the brakes.

questions.question: When a vehicle starts, warning lights and buzzers:

options.text: Should stay on for several minutes.
Should turn off within a few seconds.
Should stay on until you turn them off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should turn off within a few seconds.
questions.explanation: After the engine starts, warning lights and buzzers for oil, coolant, charging circuits, and anti-lock brakes (ABS) should go off right away.

questions.question: The "crack-the-whip" effect can:
questions.explanation: The "crack-the-whip" effect can flip a trailer during a lane change. To prevent this, make all lane changes slowly and safely.

questions.question: When uncoupling a triple trailer rig, which trailer should be uncoupled first?
questions.explanation: When uncoupling a triple trailer rig, uncouple the third trailer first. Then uncouple the remaining trailers like you normally would for a double.
